title: Start with the Dividend
先從股利說起
paras: The shareholder meeting at Cedar Foods started twenty minutes late, and Elena Kowalski, the new CFO, could feel the room watching her. Two years earlier, a larger rival had tried a hostile {{takeover|takeover}}, and the board had fought it off. The friendly {{merger|merger}} with Brightfield Grocers had calmed most people down, but not everyone.
錫達食品的股東會晚了二十分鐘才開始，新任財務長艾蓮娜・柯瓦斯基感覺得到全場的目光都落在她身上。兩年前，一家規模更大的對手曾想惡意收購公司，董事會把它擋了下來。與布萊特菲爾德超市的友善合併讓多數人安了心，但並非所有人。

Elena put up the first chart. “Our annual {{turnover|turnover}} has grown {{steadily|steadily}}. Total sales rose from $410 million to $520 million in three years,” she said. “But I won’t pretend it’s all good news. Profit fell {{sharply|sharply}} in the spring, when we closed eleven overlapping stores.”
艾蓮娜秀出第一張圖表。「我們的年營業額穩定成長。三年來總銷售額從四億一千萬美元增加到五億兩千萬美元，」她說。「不過我不會假裝全是好消息。春天的時候獲利大幅下滑，因為我們關掉了十一家商圈重疊的店。」

A retired teacher, Mr. Ortega, raised his hand. He owned a few hundred Cedar shares, a small piece of his retirement {{portfolio|portfolio}}. “My question is simple,” he said. “Will I still get my quarterly {{dividend|dividend}}?”
一位姓奧爾特加的退休教師舉起了手。他持有幾百股錫達的股票，是他退休投資組合裡小小的一部分。「我的問題很簡單，」他說。「我還領得到每季的股利嗎？」

“Yes,” Elena said. “In {{spite|spite}} of the drop in spring profit, the board decided last week to keep it at forty cents a share.” She added that the thirty {{franchise|franchise}} stores, run by local owners under the Cedar name, had done well. A long round of questions {{precede|preceded}} the shareholders’ vote on the dividend, and Mr. Ortega asked three more. When the vote finally came, it passed easily. In the hallway afterward he shook her hand. “Next time,” he said, smiling, “start with the dividend.”
「可以，」艾蓮娜說。「儘管春天的獲利下滑，董事會上週已決定維持每股四十美分。」她接著說，三十家由當地業主以錫達名義經營的加盟店表現很好。股東對股利表決之前，先有一輪很長的提問，奧爾特加先生又多問了三個問題。表決終於進行時，輕鬆過關。會後在走廊上，他和她握了握手。「下次啊，」他笑著說，「先從股利講起。」
